hypothesis: exp2 softmax with log2(e) folded into the scale: in every attention kernel (_attn_fwd prefill/small, _attn_fwd_split decode) keep the raw qk = tl.dot(q, k), use qk_scale = scale * log2(e), compute m_new = max(m_i, rowmax(qk) * qk_scale) and p = exp2(qk * qk_scale - m_new), alpha = exp2(m_i - m_new). The split kernel stores its LSE in the log2 domain (m_i + log2(l_i)) and the combine kernel weights splits with exp2, so the math stays consistent. No tile/schedule changes.
rationale: HEAD profile on prefill_8192: winning config is BLOCK_M=128 w8 (256 threads, 223 regs, 1 block/SM, 16.7% occupancy), SM throughput only 37.6%, L2 hit 96%, DRAM 1.8% -> prefill is issue/compute-limited inside the CTA, and prefill rows are the weakest (~0.92-0.93x FA2) while decode is 1.02-1.5x. Per score element the current loop does mul(scale), sub(max), and tl.exp (which lowers to mul by log2e + ex2.approx); with exp2 and the scale folded the multiply-subtract becomes one FFMA feeding ex2 directly, removing ~2 FP32 ops per element from the softmax which competes with the mma.sync issue slots. With only 8 warps per SM there is little latency hiding, so trimming the non-MMA instruction stream should translate fairly directly into prefill time.
expected_effect: Prefill rows ~3-7% faster (towards ~0.97-1.0x FA2); decode unchanged (memory-bound). Geomean up ~2-4%.
